title: Aggregate Power Flexibility in Unbalanced Distribution Systems
authors: Xin Chen; Emiliano Dall'Anese; Changhong Zhao; Na Li
focus: Aggregate flexibility region in distribution systems
explicit_contribution: Develops distribution-level power aggregation strategies for DER flexibility under unbalanced-network constraints.
project_inference: Shows that unbalanced-network aggregate flexibility itself is established prior art; EV-FLEX-BIAS novelty must be about transfer of an already-computed balanced schedule, schedule-specific loss, repair, or fast screening rather than first studying unbalanced flexibility.

title: Quantifying Phase Unbalance and Coordination Impacts on Distribution Network Flexibility
authors: Andrey Churkin; Wangwei Kong; Pierluigi Mancarella; Eduardo A. Martinez Cesena
focus: Impact of phase unbalance and coordination assumptions on aggregate DER flexibility
validation: illustrative 5-bus and real 221-bus UK LV network
explicit_contribution: Explicitly models voltage-unbalance and phase-coordination constraints and reports that a substantial share of aggregate flexibility can become unavailable because of unbalance and lack of coordination.
project_inference: Direct support for separating fixed-schedule transferability loss from coordination-repairable loss; strong motivation for an alpha_fixed vs alpha_repaired analysis.

title: Coordinated Deliverable Energy Flexibility from EV Aggregators in Distribution Networks
explicit_contribution: Uses a DSO model to determine deliverable EV energy flexibility under grid constraints and uncertainty, followed by aggregator charging-schedule optimization.
project_inference: Directly supports the distinction between nominal aggregator flexibility and grid-deliverable flexibility; differs from EV-FLEX-BIAS because it optimizes deliverable flexibility rather than replaying a precomputed balanced schedule.

title: Computation of Robust Dynamic Operating Envelopes Based on Non-convex OPF for Unbalanced Distribution Networks
focus: Robust dynamic operating envelopes in unbalanced networks
explicit_contribution: Proposes sensitivity filtering to reduce the computational burden of robust DOE calculation using non-convex unbalanced three-phase OPF and compares accuracy/efficiency considerations with linearized approaches.
project_inference: Strong baseline/method-lineage support for adding a physics/sensitivity screening comparator rather than comparing PHiCTE only with empirical derating rules.

title: Optimizing Phase Allocation in Unbalanced Power Distribution Networks using a Linearized DistFlow Formulation
authors: Rahul K. Gupta; Daniel K. Molzahn
focus: Phase allocation in unbalanced distribution networks
explicit_contribution: Develops a MILP phase-allocation method based on linearized DistFlow and phase-consistency constraints for unbalanced networks affected by single-phase devices including EV chargers.
project_inference: Supports phase-aware repair/reallocation as a physically grounded mitigation concept; it does not by itself establish EV schedule repair under fixed aggregator commitments.

title: Linear Phase Balancing Scheme using Voltage Unbalance Sensitivities in Multi-phase Power Distribution Grids
focus: Sensitivity-based phase balancing and VUF linearization
explicit_contribution: Linearizes voltage-unbalance metrics including VUF using first-order Taylor approximations and applies the sensitivities in a feedback phase-balancing control scheme.
project_inference: Supports a local-sensitivity physics baseline for fast screening of fixed schedule rays, particularly for VUF-related constraints.

title: Coordinated Dynamic Operating Envelopes for Unlocking Additional Flexibility at Grid Edge
authors: Ali Jalilian; Deepjyoti Deka; Md. Umar Hashmi; Dirk Van Hertem
focus: Operating envelopes with partially coordinated resources
explicit_contribution: Constructs coordinated/robust DOEs and reports that partial coordination can unlock additional aggregate active-power range relative to non-coordinated allocation.
project_inference: Recent evidence that coordination changes usable flexibility and should be treated as a first-class experimental factor rather than only a limitation.

title: Bayesian Active Learning-Based Soft Data Space Calibration for System-Wise Aggregate Flexibility Characterization
authors: Shengyi Wang; Liang Du; Xin Chen
validation: system-wise aggregate flexibility experiments reported in paper
explicit_contribution: Addresses the computational burden of accurately characterizing system-wide aggregate power flexibility using Bayesian active-learning-based soft data-space calibration.
project_inference: Shows that modern flexibility research explicitly values computationally efficient surrogate/calibration methods; motivates benchmarking EV-FLEX-BIAS screening against stronger modern approximations, not only simple global/feeder derating.
